measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: length of the bolt under the head (the threaded shank)

measures.reply: webcam bolt length: about 10 mm (under the head); camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.what: is the slot longer or shorter than a bank card's long edge (about 85 mm)?
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: look inside: is there a spring-loaded pin or button sticking out of the floor or a jaw? If yes, roughly how far from the end of the slot, and how thick is it?
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

limitations.blocked_by: the bolt's ~10 mm shank and ~15 mm head: recessing that head into the underside of a 38 mm-wide Arca dovetail leaves the seating ring too thin, and the resulting 6-7 mm of thread engagement risks bottoming out in the camera socket (socket depth couldn't be measured)
limitations.wanted: Reuse the salvaged 1/4-20 webcam-mount bolt as the camera screw, so the camera hangs on a metal thread in its metal socket
limitations.why: A metal screw would be stronger and re-usable; instead the design uses an integral printed 1/4-20 post with 5 mm engagement, the same as commercial quick-release plates

limitations.blocked_by: no usable measurements came back for the safety pin (position/size unknown)
limitations.wanted: Model the spring-pin safety notch that many drop-in Arca clamps need in the plate's underside
limitations.why: Without the pin's position the notch can't be placed reliably; the manual covers it as a drill-or-melt step instead

limitations.wanted: PETG or ABS for the plate (better heat and wear resistance for a load-bearing quick-release plate)
limitations.why: The plate is temporary, but PLA softens in a hot car and wears faster against the clamp jaws
